hints: Identify the two mutually exclusive circumstances under which Sam gets a cup of coffee: when the bus is on time, or when the bus is not on time.

Multiply along each path using conditional probabilities: $\mathrm{P}(\text{on time}) \times \mathrm{P}(\text{coffee} \mid \text{on time})$ and $\mathrm{P}(\text{late}) \times \mathrm{P}(\text{coffee} \mid \text{late})$.
Add the probabilities of these two disjoint branches.
walkthrough:
Define the events $T$ (bus is on time) and $C$ (Sam gets a cup of coffee), and partition the event $C$ into two mutually exclusive branches:
$$\mathrm{P}(C) = \mathrm{P}(T \cap C) + \mathrm{P}(T' \cap C)$$

Apply the multiplication rule using the given probabilities $\mathrm{P}(T) = 0.6$, $\mathrm{P}(T') = 1 - 0.6 = 0.4$, $\mathrm{P}(C \mid T) = 0.9$, and $\mathrm{P}(C \mid T') = 0.3$:
$$\mathrm{P}(T \cap C) = \mathrm{P}(T) \times \mathrm{P}(C \mid T) = 0.6 \times 0.9 = 0.54$$
$$\mathrm{P}(T' \cap C) = \mathrm{P}(T') \times \mathrm{P}(C \mid T') = 0.4 \times 0.3 = 0.12$$

Sum the branch probabilities to obtain the total probability that Sam gets coffee:
$$\mathrm{P}(C) = 0.54 + 0.12 = 0.66$$
teacher_walkthrough: Notice that there are two distinct scenarios where the student buys coffee:

Scenario 1 (Bus is on time and student buys coffee): Multiply the 60% chance the bus is on time by the 90% chance of buying coffee:
$$\text{Chance} = 0.6 \times 0.9 = 0.54$$

Scenario 2 (Bus is late and student buys coffee): Multiply the 40% chance the bus is late by the 30% chance of buying coffee:
$$\text{Chance} = 0.4 \times 0.3 = 0.12$$

Add the probabilities of both scenarios to get the overall chance of buying coffee:
$$\mathrm{P}(\text{Coffee}) = 0.54 + 0.12 = 0.66\text{ (a 66\% chance)}$$

hints: State the conditional probability formula: $\mathrm{P}(T' \mid C') = \dfrac{\mathrm{P}(T' \cap C')}{\mathrm{P}(C')}$, where $T'$ means the bus is not on time and $C'$ means Sam gets no coffee.
Find the numerator: the bus is not on time ($0.4$) and Sam does not get coffee ($1 - 0.3 = 0.7$).
Find the denominator using the complement of the answer from part (i): $\mathrm{P}(C') = 1 - \mathrm{P}(C) = 1 - 0.66$.
Divide the intersection probability by $\mathrm{P}(C')$ and evaluate to 3 significant figures.
walkthrough:
Write the formula for the conditional probability that the bus is not on time ($T'$) given that Sam does not get a cup of coffee ($C'$):
$$\mathrm{P}(T' \mid C') = \dfrac{\mathrm{P}(T' \cap C')}{\mathrm{P}(C')}$$

Calculate the joint probability of the bus being late and Sam not getting coffee:
$$\mathrm{P}(T' \cap C') = \mathrm{P}(T') \times \mathrm{P}(C' \mid T') = 0.4 \times (1 - 0.3) = 0.4 \times 0.7 = 0.28$$

Calculate the denominator $\mathrm{P}(C')$ using the complement rule with the result from part (i):
$$\mathrm{P}(C') = 1 - \mathrm{P}(C) = 1 - 0.66 = 0.34$$
teacher_walkthrough: We are given that the student did not buy coffee. We want to find the probability that the bus was late.

First, find the total probability that the student did not buy coffee by taking the complement of our answer from part (i):
$$\mathrm{P}(\text{No coffee}) = 1 - 0.66 = 0.34$$

Next, calculate the probability that the bus was late and the student did not buy coffee:
$$\mathrm{P}(\text{Late and No coffee}) = 0.4 \times (1 - 0.3) = 0.4 \times 0.7 = 0.28$$

Divide the favourable outcome by the given condition to find the conditional probability:
$$\mathrm{P}(\text{Late} \mid \text{No coffee}) = \frac{0.28}{0.34} = \frac{28}{34} = \frac{14}{17} \approx 0.824$$
